light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but growth slows and the leaves stay small

items: Trained up a tree trunk or totem
landscape_use.note: Frost-free, humid zones only; keep out of direct sun

home_use.note: Likes humid air; group it with other plants or run a humidifier nearby

snap: A climbing philodendron with velvety, near-black leaves that shimmer with bronze and gold, and new leaves that open golden. It loves warmth and humid air, and its leaves grow much larger when it climbs a pole. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Native to the rainforests of Colombia, where it climbs tree trunks in warm, humid shade. Young plants carry small, heart-shaped leaves. As the vine climbs, the leaves grow longer and larger. Indoors, with a pole to climb, it can reach 1–2 m.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Give it humid air, warmth and bright indirect light. Aim for humidity of 60% or more and keep it above 15°C. Water when the top 3–5 cm of the mix is dry, use a chunky, airy mix, and never leave the pot standing in water. Direct sun fades the velvet sheen. Dry air and cold drafts turn the leaf edges brown.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The velvety leaves look almost black in some light, then glow green and bronze as you move. New leaves open golden-bronze and darken as they age. A moss pole makes the leaves bigger and longer. Dust them gently with a soft, dry brush; wiping hard or using leaf shine spoils the velvet look.
